intent: Add a shell-free native Go launcher and fetch path for distroless images (#56)
Go launcher skeleton, JavaLocator and static cross-build

name: JavaLauncherBinary
role: Static Go executable (launcher/) that will run install, fetch and app start without a shell
conditions: Built with CGO_ENABLED=0 so it needs only the kernel; verified running in FROM scratch on amd64 and arm64. A dynamic build would fail in images without a matching loader and libc, with a misleading 'no such file' error

name: JavaLocator
role: Finds the java executable the warmup jar runs on
conditions: Order: explicit path in the app command (never falls back to another JDK if missing), PATH, JAVA_HOME, well-known JDK paths. Empty PATH entries are skipped so a relative ./java is never picked up. Returns empty when none is found, which the callers treat as the fallback

subject: Cross-compiling in Docker
why: Use FROM --platform=$BUILDPLATFORM with GOARCH=$TARGETARCH so the Go compiler runs natively; emulating the target machine for the build is far slower and unnecessary. Test the amd64 binary on an arm64 host only with an image built for that platform

title: Static binary (CGO_ENABLED=0) over a dynamic build
why: A scratch or distroless image may have no loader or libc, or a different one; a static Go binary needs only the kernel, so one file works in every image
alternative: Dynamic build shipping libc in the tools image — rejected: larger, and breaks when the app image's libc differs

title: Locate java by the app's own launch command first
why: An archive is valid only for the exact JDK that runs the app, so the tool must run on that same JDK; a missing explicit path returns no java rather than silently choosing another
alternative: Always prefer JAVA_HOME — rejected: can pick a different JDK than the app uses, so the cache would never match
